unresolved_issues: Replace 'counters since stats creation' with an explicit 35.49-day window (pg_postmaster_start_time / pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset). Convert every scan count to per-day rates and add the SQL to the appendix. Also state that the pgss window is about 95.5 days (pg_stat_statements_info.stats_reset age), which differs from the table-stat window.

Rewrite the '~170 rows per PK scan = incremental extractor/CDC poller' interpretation. At about 617K rows/day (about 50% of the table/day), it is a repeated full paginated read or bulk keyed lookups, not incremental polling. Keep 'id-range pagination' only as one hypothesis.
Restate '36 seq scans = daily dump' as supported by evidence: 36 ≈ 35.49 days of uptime, and many DBs show exactly 36 xact_commit. Cite the pg_stat_database query.

Stop calling youpay seq scans 'whole-table reads' as a certainty. The average of 1,144,861 is 93% of reltuples and could mix full and partial (LIMIT-terminated) scans. Phrase it as 'consistent with mostly full-table reads'.

Grant request PII risk: kafka_giftcreationlog.error/failure (text), datalog error_data (text), and youpay response_summary are free text that commonly embeds payload fragments (emails, names, gift codes). Grant them only via a view that returns a normalized error class (for example regexp_replace of digits, emails and uuids, then left(…,60)) or a has_error flag. P1 left(error,60) and P5 left(response_summary,80) should read from that view.

P11: `g.order_id ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$' AND EXISTS(... o.id = g.order_id::bigint)` relies on AND short-circuit order, which Postgres does not guarantee. Rewrite as `CASE WHEN g.order_id ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$' THEN EXISTS(...) END` so a non-numeric order_id cannot abort the query.

Add pack queries for the missing signals: otp last_t recency buckets; django_admin_log change_message JSON key names by content_type; FX rate age and spread; currency<>cart_currency share × approved; youpay hour-of-week × approval (1% sample); webhook ip_address = sender_ip share; commandexecuter distinct operators and date-window length.

Update the Blocker paragraph figures, or mark them as drifting. The orders-DB pgss set has changed (now 18 statements; the '19 calls / 36,575 rows' statement has been evicted and the current largest per call is 4 calls / 7,700 rows). Note that the statement set turns over, which is more evidence that pgss cannot identify the extractor.
Consider granting core_remoteurlconfig (server, is_active) plus a URL-host view, and django_admin_log.object_id (not object_repr), to allow joining admin edits to order ids. Both are PII-safe.

issues: Add a prepared-queries appendix, cheap and PII-safe, to run once SELECT is granted. It should cover: status and error counts per kafka table via TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM(1) on giftcreationlog and atwork; completed_timestamp IS NULL share and p50/p95 latency per *datalog; youpay payment_status × approved × payment_gateway counts and response_summary top-N; min/max created_on via ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 on the PK; and monthly buckets via id ranges.

Downgrade the 'about one payment session per order' inference. youpay order_reference is nullable, and matching reltuples (1.229M vs 1.232M) is not evidence of 1:1. List this as a hypothesis to test with a count(DISTINCT order_reference) sample.

Reframe '2.5 gift-creation events per order'. event_id is UNIQUE, so retries (if any) are new rows rather than updates. The ratio is uninterpretable until status is profiled, and it also depends on the order_id format (number vs id vs external ref).

Add success_url, failure_url, cancel_url and verify_url to the youpay PII/secret exclusion list for the column-level grant, alongside customer_email, customer_name, name_on_card, customer_ip_address, card_bin, card_last4, the mobile numbers, session_id and the jsonb blobs.
Correct the youpay index description: card_issuer_country and qitaf_request_id have btree indexes, in addition to the 3 boolean flag indexes.

Note that pg_stat_statements is readable but query text is redacted. Recommend granting pg_read_all_stats, or reading it from the primary's monitoring, to identify the consumer running 909 seq scans on youpay.
Add a latency/SLA section to Friction & Errors, using start/completed_timestamp and created_on/modified_on deltas as measurable metrics once granted.
Warn that joining kafka_giftcreationlog.order_id to order_order must be id-range- or sample-bounded, because there is no index on order_id.
Add ygag_youpay_db and ygag_ecom_gifts_db to Cross-DB Keys and to the grant request as counterpart sources for payment and gift-creation truth.

Make the grant request concrete: a table list plus an explicit column allowlist (or PII-free views) for youpay, kafka_giftcreationlog (excluding payload and created_gift_details) and the datalogs (excluding data, or exposing only jsonb keys).

Rewrite the pg_stat_statements paragraph in the Blocker section: it is cluster-wide. Report the per-DB split (orders DB: 20 stmts / about 1.86M calls; ecomweb_stores: 4,818 / about 385M). Remove 'That includes all 38 tables in scope'. Add the per-DB query to the appendix.

Replace the 'grant pg_read_all_stats to find the 909-seq-scan consumer' recommendation. The current orders-DB pgss rows contain no statement matching about 1.14M rows per scan, and dealloc is 663,020. Recommend Performance Insights / pg_stat_activity sampling / log_min_duration_statement on the replica, and keep pg_read_all_stats only as a secondary aid.

Add the scan-ratio inference: about 1.145M rows per seq scan (full-table reads; also a live-row proxy) and about 170 rows per PK index scan (id-range pagination by an extractor). Note that the card_issuer_country, qitaf and boolean indexes are unused on the replica. Cite pg_stat_user_tables.seq_tup_read / idx_tup_fetch and pg_stat_user_indexes in the appendix.

Fix the datalog GRANT statement. As written it is invalid SQL, because the column list sits after the table list and inside a comment. Use `GRANT SELECT (id, status, error_data, start_timestamp, completed_timestamp) ON kafka_atworkkafkadatalog, kafka_plusofferkafkadatalog, ... TO <emapi_login_role>;`. Also add modified_on and event_id to the legacyfraud/blacklistgift grant (needed for retry span and idempotency checks).
Name the youpay point columns explicitly in the grant (available_points, redeemed_points, earned_point) instead of the placeholder comment, and add them to the loyalty behavior section.

Fix P8. Split it into three separate `SELECT count(*) ... WHERE <flag>` statements, which can use each boolean index, or use TABLESAMPLE. Stop calling the combined FILTER query cheap or index-backed. The card_issuer_country GROUP BY over 1.23M rows should also be sampled or explicitly timed-out-guarded.

Extend P11 to test all three candidate order_id formats in one bounded window: match on o.number, o.id::text and o.order_reference (all indexed on order_order). Note that the youpay reconciliation join should use order_order.order_reference (UNIQUE index), not payment_order_reference, which has no index.

Add PII-safe structural jsonb queries to the pack: jsonb_array_length(order_items), jsonb_array_length(order_history), jsonb_object_keys(udf1 | brand_details | webhooks message | error_message) with counts only, and never values.
